result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=without, B=with): A does what was asked. It replaces the generic dashboard with check-ins, day passes and shoe rentals, and turns the form into a real check-in task. Its main weaknesses are the made-up prices (it flags them as guesses) and empty and error messages that don't tell staff what to do next. B adds solid accessibility and a better error message, but it leaves 'Item 1', 'John Doe', 'Add New', 'Submit' and the generic cards in place. So it does not finish the page for the gym. | pass 2 (A=with, B=without): B fully reframes the screen around the desk's real work: cards for check-ins, sales and shoes out, a Check in form with day pass, member and shoe rental options, and a shoe-return action. It does invent $20 and $5 prices, though it flags them as guesses, and its empty and error messages remain thin. A keeps every generic label (Item 1, Users, Revenue, Add New, Submit, Value) and asks the user for the real ones, so it leaves the main job unfinished despite solid accessibility work and better error-recovery copy.
